section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department and SCAP records from 1946 to 1948 concerning the reform, enactment, and abrogation of Japanese legislation during the Occupation. It includes despatches and texts abrogating wartime industrial and munitions control laws, draft legislation temporarily adjusting criminal procedure to align with the new Constitution, and a comprehensive index of laws enacted by the Diet between 1945 and early 1948. Additionally, the section covers the expansion of civil liberties, the founding of the Japan Civil Liberties Union, and domestic and international controversies surrounding proposed strike bans under the National Public Service Law.

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of Law No. 49 of 1945 and Imperial Ordinance No. 19 of 1946 abrogating wartime industrial legislation.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmittal cover despatch enclosing copies of Japanese legislation abrogating wartime petroleum and industrial manufacturing control laws.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 213: Transmitting Copies of Law Abrogating Fourteen Laws and Imperial Ordinance Abrogating Twenty Supporting Ordinances

subfiles.about: Abrogates fourteen wartime industrial, munitions, and petroleum control laws while establishing transitional tax, subsidy, and compensation provisions.
subfiles.summary: Japanese statute abrogating fourteen wartime industrial control laws, including petroleum, munitions, aircraft, and machine tools manufacturing legislation, with transitional provisions.
subfiles.title: Law No. 49 of 1945: Law for the Abrogation of the Petroleum Industry Law and Other Thirteen Laws

subfiles.about: Abrogates twenty imperial ordinances enforcing wartime industrial mobilization and monopoly laws.
subfiles.summary: Imperial ordinance repealing twenty enforcement ordinances connected with wartime industrial laws, retaining temporary provisions on taxes, subsidies, and munitions compensation.
subfiles.title: Imperial Ordinance No. 19 of 1946: Abrogation of the Enforcement Ordinance of the Petroleum Industry Law and Others

subfiles.about: Notes the transmittal of a bill temporarily adjusting criminal procedure to accord with the new Constitution.
subfiles.summary: Brief memorandum note referencing discussions with Mr. Oppler regarding temporary adjustments to the Code of Criminal Procedure.
subfiles.title: File Note on Bill for Temporary Adjustment of the Code of Criminal Procedure

subfiles.about: Transmits an English draft of criminal procedure amendments and Japanese texts of fifteen other bills passed by the Diet.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding an English translation of the temporary criminal procedure adjustment bill and Japanese texts of fifteen Diet bills.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 986: Drafts of an Additional Sixteen Bills Passed by the 92nd Session of the Japanese Diet

subfiles.about: Sets forth temporary modifications to criminal procedures to conform with constitutional protections for the accused.
subfiles.summary: Draft legislation establishing judicial warrants, counsel for indigent defendants, bans on coerced confessions, cross-examination rights, and appellate rules under the new Constitution.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 986: Bill for the Temporary Adjustment of the Code of Criminal Procedure Pursuant to the Enforcement of the Constitution of Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP Government Section index of laws enacted by the Diet from the start of the Occupation through February 5, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch enclosing copies of an index to the Official Gazette listing laws enacted during the Allied Occupation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 89: Official Gazette Index to Laws Enacted by the Japanese Diet During the Occupation

subfiles.about: Compiles a comprehensive index of 391 laws, ordinances, and budgets enacted across five Diet sessions under the Allied Occupation.
subfiles.from: R. G. Brown, Capt., F.A., Legislative Division, Government Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive index lists 391 statutes, imperial ordinances, and budgets passed by the Japanese Diet from the 89th session through the 1st National Diet. The enactments are categorized by sponsoring ministry or cabinet board, providing Official Gazette numbers, enactment dates, and legislative titles.
subfiles.title: Official Gazette Index to Laws Enacted by Diet During Occupation to Date

subfiles.about: Routes a legislative amendment bill within the Department of State.
subfiles.from: FE - NA (Division of Northeast Asian Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Internal Department of State routing slip transmitting an amendment bill between geographic and records divisions.
subfiles.title: Standard Form No. 64: Routing Slip from FE - NA to DC/R

subfiles.about: Amends revenue transfer amounts from the General Account to cover 1947 fiscal year deficits in several special accounts.
subfiles.summary: Draft bill adjusting yen appropriations transferred from the General Account to cover deficits in government railway, communications, and insurance special accounts.
subfiles.title: Revised Bill to Amend A Part of Law No. 170 of 1947

subfiles.about: Reports on fifteen major laws expanding Japanese civil liberties and the rapid growth of the Japan Civil Liberties Union.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch analyzing new legislation expanding Japanese civil liberties, Dr. Alfred Oppler's public education efforts, and the formation and activities of the Japan Civil Liberties Union.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 524: New Laws Expanding Japanese Civil Liberties

subfiles.about: Highlights statements by Dr. Alfred C. Oppler regarding newly enacted civil liberties laws and the need for public awareness.
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.summary: Far East Command press release summarizing major judicial reforms—including habeas corpus, criminal procedure, and juvenile protections—and urging citizens to defend their constitutional rights.
subfiles.title: Press Release No. 1630: Few Japanese Aware of New Rights Dr. Oppler Points Out

subfiles.about: Details the establishment, leadership, committee structure, and nationwide campaign of the Japan Civil Liberties Union.
subfiles.from: Shinkichi Unno, Director-General, Japanese Civil Liberties Union (Nippon Times)
subfiles.summary: Newspaper article by Shinkichi Unno tracing the formation of the Japan Civil Liberties Union following Roger Baldwin's visit, detailing its organization, regional branches, and human rights missions.
subfiles.title: Nippon Times Article: Civil Liberties Union Here Growing into Big Movement

subfiles.about: Reports on Soviet diplomatic and political backing of Japanese communist opposition to anti-strike revisions of the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This despatch details meetings between Soviet officials and the Democracy Protection League opposing restrictions on government workers' right to strike. It analyzes Soviet interference in domestic Japanese politics and direct liaison with communist organizations in violation of Occupation objectives.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 621: Soviet Support of Communist Opposition to Revision of National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Transmits a British Embassy memorandum expressing UK reservations about proposed strike bans in the National Public Service and Public Corporation Bills.
subfiles.summary: Outgoing telegram communicating British views to SCAP suggesting arbitration and a cooling-off period rather than an absolute ban on strikes by public employees.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 404: UK Views on National Public Service Bill
